content: If you are experiencing a side effect from a medication, you can report it to the FDA through their MedWatch program at www.fda.gov/medwatch or by calling 1-800-FDA-1088. In Canada, you can report side effects to Health Canada’s MedEffect program by calling 1-866-234-2345. Serious Side Effects of Vaginal Metronidazole Although rare, vaginal metronidazole can cause serious side effects. Below are the most significant ones and what to do if they occur: Severe Allergic Reactions Vaginal metronidazole may trigger serious allergic reactions. Stop using the medication immediately and seek medical attention if you experience any of the following symptoms: Difficulty breathing or wheezing Rapid heartbeat Fever or a general feeling of being unwell Swollen lymph nodes Swelling of the face, lips, mouth, tongue, or throat Difficulty swallowing or a sensation of throat tightness Itching, skin rash, or hives (pale red bumps on the skin) Nausea or vomiting Dizziness, lightheadedness, or fainting Stomach cramps Joint pain Nervous System Problems Other forms of metronidazole (oral or injectable) have been associated with nervous system issues. Stop using vaginal metronidazole and contact your healthcare provider if you experience: Seizures Numbness, tingling, or pain in the hands or feet (peripheral neuropathy) Confusion, difficulty thinking, or behavioral changes Precautions: Who Should Not Use Vaginal Metronidazole? Allergies to Ingredients Do not use vaginal metronidazole if you are allergic to: Metronidazole Nuvesse Vandazole Parabens Any other nitroimidazole derivatives Any ingredients in the specific product dispensed (your pharmacist can provide a full list of ingredients) Drug Interactions Vaginal metronidazole should not be used with certain medications. Inform your healthcare provider about all prescription and over-the-counter (OTC) medications, vitamins, minerals, herbal products, and supplements you are taking. Specific interactions include: Warfarin (Coumadin): A blood thinner used to treat blood clots Disulfiram (Antabuse): Used to treat alcoholism, especially if taken within the past two weeks Lithium (Eskalith, Lithobid): Used to treat bipolar disorder Alcohol Avoid consuming alcohol or foods containing alcohol or propylene glycol while using vaginal metronidazole and for at least one day after stopping Nuvesse or three days after stopping Vandazole. Combining alcohol with this medication can lead to serious side effects. Important Usage Information Use vaginal metronidazole only if prescribed by a healthcare provider. Follow the prescribed dosage and instructions carefully. Do not share this medication with others, even if they have the same condition, as it may harm them. Keep the medication out of reach of children. Avoid sexual activity and the use of vaginal products (e.g., tampons or douches) while using vaginal metronidazole. This medication is for vaginal use only. If it comes into contact with your eyes, rinse them with cool water and contact your healthcare provider. Before Using Vaginal Metronidazole Inform your healthcare provider about: Any nervous system conditions, such as seizures or peripheral neuropathy All medications, vitamins, minerals, herbal products, and supplements you are taking If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding Pregnancy The effects of vaginal metronidazole on pregnancy and unborn babies are not fully known. Discuss with your healthcare provider whether it is safe to use this medication during pregnancy. Breastfeeding Vaginal metronidazole passes into breast milk. If you are breastfeeding, you may need to pump and discard your breast milk while using the medication and for two days after completing treatment. Consult your healthcare provider for guidance. Overdose If you or someone else uses too much vaginal metronidazole, seek immediate medical attention by calling 911 or contacting a Poison Control Center at 1-800-222-1222. Missed Dose If you miss a dose, use it as soon as you remember. If it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not use double or extra doses. Complete the full prescribed course of treatment, even if your symptoms improve, to reduce the risk of future infections becoming resistant to this medication. Additional Notes Always consult your healthcare provider for the most accurate and up-to-date information regarding your treatment. If you have questions about your medication or its interactions, your pharmacist or healthcare provider can provide detailed guidance.
